fatal_errors: The proposed single-phase CrMnFeCoNi alloy does not match the target as-cast, dual-phase FCC+B2 AlCoCrFeNi2.1 eutectic HEA.
Cooling-rate-controlled grain-boundary clustering replaces the target intervention of aging within an approximately 550–750°C temperature window.

The grain-boundary decohesion mechanism misses the target mechanism involving enhanced L12 ordering, elevated APB energy, restricted cross-slip, planar slip, and stress concentration at jagged FCC/B2 phase-boundary tips.
The hypothesis does not predict the target non-monotonic ductile–brittle–ductile response, including minimum ductility after 600°C aging and recovery after 750°C aging.
Its grain-boundary segregation mechanism resembles the conventional grain-boundary embrittlement expectation rather than providing the intended phase-boundary-based contrast.
explanation: This is a scientifically credible alternative hypothesis for intermediate-temperature ductility loss in CrMnFeCoNi. The cited evidence directly supports Cr/Ni/Mn grain-boundary nanoclustering, reduced cohesion, and intergranular cracking near 700°C. The APT-plus-mechanical-testing design is measurable and includes a reasonably decisive falsification rule, although the claimed dependence on cooling rate is not established by the supplied evidence and may introduce processing confounders. Reconstruction of the hidden target is poor: the material, initial microstructure, thermal treatment, structural mediator, crack-initiation site, and predicted temperature dependence are all different. Only the broad themes of HEA embrittlement and an intermediate-temperature brittle regime overlap. Thus, it is best classified as a plausible evidence-backed alternative rather than a reconstruction.
